investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on 6-Node Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T09:28–09:35Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would write those fields.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes had insufficient remaining VM resource allocations, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for the full timeout window (~120–150 s), the eval runner surfaced the scheduler message as the check failure and produced an empty evidence object, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be missing and both contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf running/idle/ready) to go unevaluated. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, no remote agent VM was ever provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), which submits a pod that never starts, so the probe never reaches the runtime response stage and produces no evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes satisfy, so even if VM capacity were freed those 4 nodes would still be ineligible. This is a contributing constraint visible in the same scheduler message.

TERTIARY — a prior eval run or unrelated workload consumed the last VM slots and was not cleaned up before this run started, leaving zero free slots at probe time. The sequential failure order (remote-agent-create at 09:30, remote-agent-state at 09:33, remote-agent-runtime at 09:35) is consistent with each probe independently hitting the same exhausted pool.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — a cluster scaling or node provisioning event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes from a higher count to exactly 2, shrinking total VM capacity. No node-count change evidence is present in the packet; this remains speculative.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity remaining on the 2 eligible nodes, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission controller issue would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks passed on an immediately subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a brief capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a node label that no longer exists), the root cause would shift from VM capacity exhaustion to a configuration drift problem.

If no pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of failure, the exhaustion diagnosis would be weakened and a node-level resource accounting bug or admission webhook issue would become the primary hypothesis.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the shared infrastructure exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the failure would be localized to the runtime probe specifically.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a minimal pod spec at a higher frequency (e.g., every 5 minutes) to detect VM slot exhaustion earlier in the degradation curve rather than only at full outage.
